main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic properties of fabrics used in cloth and garment construction
learning_activity_name: Describe textile fibres, yarn and fabric (meaning, classification and properties)
sla_assessment_criteria: Textile fibres, yarns and fabrics are described clearly.
sla_teaching_aids: Pictures/diagram of textile fibres|Yarns|Fabrics|Chart of classification of textile fibres|Yarn
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Textile fibres, yarns and fabrics are the basic building blocks of any garment, and understanding their meaning and classification is the foundation of textile study.
sla_notes_details: A textile fibre is the smallest hair-like unit of raw material that can be spun into yarn, a yarn is a continuous strand formed by twisting fibres together, and a fabric is a flexible material made by weaving, knitting or otherwise interlacing yarns (or, for non-woven fabrics, bonding fibres directly). Fibres are classified by source into natural fibres, plant fibres such as cotton and linen, and animal fibres such as wool and silk, and man-made fibres, further split into regenerated fibres such as rayon (made from natural cellulose) and synthetic fibres such as polyester and nylon (made from chemicals). Key properties considered for each fibre include strength, elasticity, absorbency, durability and how the fibre responds to heat, which together determine the fabric's comfort, care requirements and suitability for a given garment.
sla_notes_illustrations: Cotton, a natural plant fibre, is comfortable and absorbent, making it suitable for everyday shirts, while polyester, a synthetic fibre, is strong and wrinkle-resistant, making it suitable for garments that need to hold their shape.
sla_notes_daily_life: Every piece of clothing a person wears, from a school uniform to a kanga, is made from fibres and yarns that have first been classified and selected for their suitable properties.
sla_exercise: Define a textile fibre.::The smallest hair-like unit of raw material that can be spun into yarn.||Name the two main classes of textile fibres.::Natural fibres and man-made fibres.||Give one example each of a natural and a man-made fibre.::Cotton (natural) and polyester (man-made).

learning_activity_name: Perform different tests to identify types of fibres using different methods (physical inspection, microscope, burning, chemical)
sla_name: Testing methods to identify types of fibres
sla_assessment_criteria: Different tests for identifying types of fibres are performed correctly using different methods.
sla_teaching_aids: Various types of fibres|Chemicals|Hand lens|Microscope|Source of fire
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Because many fibres look similar, specific tests are used to correctly identify the fibre content of a fabric sample.
sla_notes_details: Common fibre identification methods include physical inspection (examining the fibre's length, lustre, strength and feel by hand), microscopic examination (viewing the fibre's cross-section and longitudinal shape under a microscope, since each fibre type has a distinctive appearance, for example cotton appears twisted and ribbon-like), the burning test (observing how a small fibre sample burns, the smell produced, and the type of ash or residue left, since natural cellulose fibres like cotton burn quickly with a paper-like smell leaving soft grey ash, while synthetic fibres like polyester melt, shrink from the flame, and leave a hard bead), and chemical tests (applying specific reagents that react differently with different fibre types, such as solubility in certain acids). Combining more than one method gives a more reliable identification.
sla_notes_illustrations: When a small thread from an unknown fabric is held to a flame and it melts into a hard black bead with an acrid, chemical smell rather than burning to soft ash, this burning test result identifies the fibre as synthetic, likely polyester or nylon.
sla_notes_daily_life: Textile quality inspectors, and even a shopper checking whether a garment label's fibre content is accurate, use these same identification methods.
sla_exercise: Name the four main methods used to identify types of fibres.::Physical inspection, microscopic examination, the burning test, and chemical tests.||What result would the burning test give for a pure cotton fibre?::It burns quickly with a paper-like smell, leaving soft grey ash.||Why is microscopic examination useful for identifying fibres?::Each fibre type has a distinctive cross-sectional and longitudinal shape visible under a microscope.

learning_activity_name: Describe different methods of fabric and garment decoration
sla_name: Methods of fabric and garment decoration
sla_assessment_criteria: Different methods of decorating fabrics and garments are described correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Audio visual clips|Sample for different decorated fabrics|Garments
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Fabric and garment decoration adds visual interest, personal expression and value to plain textile materials.
sla_notes_details: Methods of decorating fabrics and garments include dyeing (applying colour throughout the fibre or fabric using dye baths), printing (applying colour or pattern to the fabric surface using techniques such as screen printing, block printing or batik), painting (applying colour by hand using brushes, fabric paints or colour paste to create unique designs), embroidery (stitching decorative thread designs onto fabric), applique (attaching cut pieces of fabric onto a base fabric to form a design), and quilting (stitching layers of fabric together, often with padding, to create a raised, textured pattern). Each method suits different purposes, materials and levels of durability required.
sla_notes_illustrations: A tailor decorating a plain white kitenge might use batik printing to create a repeating wax-resist pattern before dyeing, while another might choose hand embroidery to add a floral design around the neckline of a blouse.
sla_notes_daily_life: Decorated kangas, embroidered kanzu and hand-painted T-shirts sold in Tanzanian markets are everyday products created using these same fabric decoration methods.
sla_exercise: Name three methods of decorating fabric.::Dyeing, printing and embroidery (or painting, applique, quilting).||What is the difference between dyeing and printing?::Dyeing applies colour throughout the fibre or fabric, while printing applies colour or pattern only to the fabric surface.||What is applique?::A decoration method where cut pieces of fabric are attached onto a base fabric to form a design.

sla_notes_intro: This competence applies the theory of fabric decoration practically, producing a decorated fabric using dyeing, printing or painting.
sla_notes_details: Dyeing a fabric involves preparing the dye bath (mixing dye, water and any fixing agents such as soda ash), pre-treating the fabric (washing to remove finishes that could resist dye), immersing the fabric evenly in the dye bath for the required time, then rinsing and drying. Printing, such as screen printing, involves preparing a screen with the desired design, applying paste or ink through the screen with a squeegee onto the fabric, and curing the print with heat to make it permanent. Painting involves sketching or stencilling a design directly onto the fabric and applying fabric paint carefully with a brush, allowing layers to dry between colours to avoid muddying the design.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student tie-dyeing a plain white T-shirt would twist and bind sections of the fabric with rubber bands before dipping it into a dye bath, so the bound areas resist the dye and create a distinctive pattern once untied and dried.
sla_notes_daily_life: Small businesses producing tie-dyed and batik kitenge for sale in local markets use exactly these dyeing, printing and painting techniques to add value to plain fabric.
sla_exercise: Why is fabric usually pre-treated (washed) before dyeing?::To remove finishes on the fabric that could otherwise resist the dye and cause uneven colouring.||What tool is used to apply ink or paste through a screen during screen printing?::A squeegee.||Why should a painted fabric design be allowed to dry between colour layers?::To prevent the colours from mixing or becoming muddy.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
learning_activity_name: Use decorated fabric to construct own garment taking into consideration elements and principles of design
sla_name: Constructing a garment using decorated fabric
sla_assessment_criteria: Garments are constructed properly using the decorated fabric taking into considerations the elements and principles of design.
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Constructing a garment from decorated fabric requires applying elements and principles of design so the finished garment looks balanced and visually appealing.
sla_notes_details: Elements of design considered include colour, line, shape, texture and pattern, while principles of design include balance, proportion, rhythm, emphasis and harmony. When constructing a garment from decorated fabric, the maker must plan pattern placement so that motifs are positioned attractively (for example, centred on a bodice rather than cut awkwardly at a seam), choose a garment style that complements the fabric's pattern scale (large motifs suit simpler garment shapes), and cut and sew the garment using standard construction techniques (cutting on grain, seam allowances, appropriate stitching) while preserving the decoration's visual impact.
sla_notes_illustrations: A tailor constructing a dress from a large-motif printed fabric would centre a bold flower motif on the front bodice as a focal point (an example of emphasis), rather than allowing the motif to be split awkwardly across a side seam.
sla_notes_daily_life: Local tailors and fashion designers who make garments from kitenge, ensuring the fabric's pattern lines up attractively at the seams, are applying exactly these same design principles daily.
sla_exercise: Name two elements of design considered when constructing a garment from decorated fabric.::Colour and pattern (or line, shape, texture).||Why is pattern placement important when cutting a garment from decorated fabric?::So that motifs are positioned attractively on the finished garment rather than cut awkwardly at a seam.||What principle of design is illustrated when a bold motif is deliberately centred on a garment's bodice?::Emphasis, drawing the eye to a chosen focal point.

specific_competence_name: Design and construct traditional clothing from selected ethnic groups in Tanzania
learning_activity_name: Explore traditional garments from selected ethnic groups in Tanzania (materials and designs used)
sla_name: Traditional garments from selected ethnic groups in Tanzania
sla_assessment_criteria: Traditional garments from different tribes are explored correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Chart or pictures showing different traditional garments|Video clips showing culture for different tribes|Online/offline sources
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Tanzania's many ethnic groups have distinct traditional garments, each with its own materials, designs and cultural meaning.
sla_notes_details: Exploring traditional garments involves identifying the ethnic group of origin, the materials traditionally used (such as bark cloth, animal hide, handwoven cotton or beadwork), the design features (colours, patterns, draping style) and the cultural context in which the garment is worn, such as ceremonies, everyday wear or status symbols. Examples include the Maasai's red shuka cloth and beaded ornaments, the kanga and kitenge widely worn across coastal and mainland communities, and various tribal ceremonial dress that use specific colours or patterns to signify age group, marital status or clan identity. Research uses online and offline sources, interviews with community elders, and museum or cultural centre visits.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student researching Maasai traditional dress would identify the red and check-patterned shuka cloth, together with beaded jewellery, as key features, and learn that red is associated with bravery and identity within Maasai culture.
sla_notes_daily_life: Traditional garments are still worn at weddings, cultural festivals and everyday life in many Tanzanian communities, giving students living examples to study directly.
sla_exercise: Name one traditional Tanzanian garment and the ethnic group associated with it.::The Maasai shuka (or kanga/kitenge worn widely across many communities).||What information should be identified when exploring a traditional garment?::Its ethnic group of origin, the materials used, the design features, and the cultural context in which it is worn.||Name one source that can be used to research traditional garments.::Online/offline sources (or interviews with community elders, or a museum/cultural centre visit).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
specific_competence_name: Design and construct traditional clothing from selected ethnic groups in Tanzania
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: This competence turns research on traditional garments into a practical construction project, producing an actual traditional garment.
sla_notes_details: Constructing a selected traditional garment involves choosing one researched traditional design, selecting suitable materials and accessories that match the original (such as specific fabric colours, beads or trims), taking accurate measurements, drafting or adapting a pattern that reflects the traditional garment's shape and construction method, and sewing the garment while preserving its authentic features. Care is taken to respect the cultural significance of the design, using appropriate colours, symbols or construction techniques associated with that ethnic group.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student constructing a Maasai-inspired garment would select red and checked fabric, add beaded trim to reflect authentic ornamentation, and cut and sew the garment in the traditional draped style rather than a modern fitted style.
sla_notes_daily_life: Tailors who make traditional wedding or ceremonial garments for Tanzanian communities apply this same combination of research, material selection and authentic construction.
sla_exercise: What should be selected to match the original design before constructing a traditional garment?::Suitable materials and accessories, such as specific fabric colours, beads or trims.||Why is it important to preserve authentic features when constructing a traditional garment?::To respect the cultural significance and identity associated with that ethnic group's design.||Name one step involved in constructing a traditional garment after selecting materials.::Taking accurate measurements and drafting or adapting a pattern (then sewing the garment).

sla_name: Creating fabric design patterns using CAD/CAM/CIM
sla_assessment_criteria: Fabric design pattens are created correctly using CAD/CAM/CIM system.
sla_teaching_aids: Computer|CAD/CAM/CIM software’s|Books|Catalogue instructional manuals|Interactive tools/audio visual tutorials
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Computer technology allows textile designers to create fabric design patterns digitally, offering speed, precision and easy experimentation compared with manual methods.
sla_notes_details: CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software allows a designer to create graphic representations of fabric designs, including regular repeating patterns and colourways, by drawing or importing a motif and using tools to repeat, resize, recolour or arrange it across a virtual fabric surface. CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing) and CIM (Computer-Integrated Manufacturing) extend this by connecting the digital design directly to production machinery, such as digital printers or cutting machines, so the approved design can be manufactured with minimal manual intervention. Creating a fabric design pattern involves selecting or drawing a motif, setting the repeat type (such as a straight or half-drop repeat), choosing a colour palette, and previewing how the pattern will look on the finished fabric before production.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student designing a kitenge pattern digitally might draw a single flower motif, then use the software's repeat tool to tile it evenly across a virtual fabric length, testing different colour combinations before finalising the design for printing.
sla_notes_daily_life: Textile companies producing branded kitenge and school uniform fabric increasingly design their patterns using CAD software before sending the files to CAM-controlled printing machines.
sla_exercise: What does CAD stand for in textile design?::Computer-Aided Design.||What is the role of CAM/CIM in fabric design production?::Connecting the digital design directly to manufacturing machinery so it can be produced with minimal manual intervention.||Name one decision made when creating a fabric design pattern using CAD.::Choosing the repeat type (or selecting a colour palette, or drawing the motif).

sla_name: Producing prototypes of various fabric designs

sla_teaching_aids: Printing machine for producing decorated designs
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A prototype is a sample version of a fabric design produced to test how the digital design translates into an actual physical fabric before full production.
sla_notes_details: Producing prototypes of fabric designs using CAM/CIM systems involves finalising the digital design file, sending it to a compatible printing or production machine, selecting the correct fabric and settings for the chosen printing method, running a small test print, and examining the physical prototype for accuracy of colour, scale and pattern alignment compared with the digital design. Adjustments are made to the digital file if the prototype reveals problems, and the process is repeated until the prototype meets the required standard before any larger production run is approved.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student who designed a repeating leaf pattern digitally would print a small prototype swatch, then check whether the leaf colours and spacing appear as intended on real fabric, adjusting the design file if the green shade printed differently than expected on screen.
sla_notes_daily_life: Fabric manufacturers always produce and approve a physical prototype swatch before committing to printing large rolls of fabric for sale, exactly as practised in this competence.
sla_exercise: What is a prototype in the context of fabric design?::A sample version of a design produced to test how it looks on actual physical fabric before full production.||Why is a test print of a prototype important before full production?::It reveals whether the colour, scale and pattern alignment match the digital design, allowing corrections before a larger, costlier run.||What should be done if a prototype reveals a problem with the design?::The digital design file is adjusted and the prototype process is repeated until the result meets the required standard.

sla_name: Preparing a portfolio of prototypes of textile products
sla_assessment_criteria: Portfolio for keeping prototype of textile products made properly.
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A portfolio brings together samples of all the practical textile work completed during the course, presented as evidence of skill and learning.
sla_notes_details: Preparing a portfolio of prototypes of textile products involves collecting and organising physical samples created during the year, such as fibre and yarn samples, printed and dyed fabric samples, fabric design patterns, and garment patterns, mounting or storing each sample neatly (for example on labelled card or in a portfolio folder), and arranging them in a logical order, often matching the order the skills were learned. Each sample should be labelled with relevant information such as the technique used and the date created, so the portfolio clearly documents the range of skills developed.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student preparing their portfolio would mount a labelled cotton fibre sample, a small piece of tie-dyed fabric, a printed pattern swatch, and a garment pattern piece onto separate labelled cards, then arrange them in a folder in the order these skills were taught.
sla_notes_daily_life: Tailors and textile designers build similar sample portfolios to show prospective clients or employers examples of their range of techniques and quality of work.
sla_exercise: What items are typically included in a textile portfolio of prototypes?::Fibre and yarn samples, printed and dyed fabric samples, fabric design patterns and garment patterns.||Why should each sample in a portfolio be labelled?::So the portfolio clearly documents which technique was used and when, showing the range of skills developed.||In what order are portfolio samples usually arranged?::In a logical order, often matching the order the skills were learned during the course.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic properties of fabrics used in cloth and garment construction
learning_activity_name: Perform different tests on fabrics (tensile strength, tear strength, pilling, colourfastness, dimensional stability)
sla_assessment_criteria: Different tests on fabrics are performed clearly.
sla_teaching_aids: Fabric samples|Salt|Washing agents|CDs with short video|Water containers|Rubbing surface|Online/offline sources
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Beyond identifying fibre type, more advanced tests assess how well a finished fabric will perform in actual use, such as its strength, colour retention and stability.
sla_notes_details: Tensile strength testing measures the force a fabric can withstand before it tears when pulled, indicating durability. Tear strength testing measures how easily a small cut or weak point in the fabric spreads into a larger tear. Pilling tests assess how much a fabric develops small balls of fibre on its surface after rubbing or wear, which affects appearance over time. Colourfastness tests check whether a fabric's dye bleeds or fades when exposed to washing, light or rubbing (crocking). Dimensional stability tests measure how much a fabric shrinks or stretches after washing or exposure to moisture and heat. Each test uses standard equipment and procedures, and results are compared with acceptable standards for the fabric's intended use.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student performing a simple colourfastness test would rub a dry white cloth against a coloured fabric sample and observe whether colour transfers onto the white cloth, indicating poor colourfastness that could cause the coloured fabric to bleed onto other clothes during washing.
sla_notes_daily_life: Consumers checking whether a new dark-coloured garment will bleed colour during its first wash, often by washing it separately, are informally applying the same colourfastness principle tested formally in the laboratory.
sla_exercise: What does a tensile strength test measure?::The force a fabric can withstand before it tears when pulled.||What is a colourfastness test used to check?::Whether a fabric's dye bleeds or fades when exposed to washing, light or rubbing.||Why is a dimensional stability test important for a fabric?::It shows how much the fabric will shrink or stretch after washing or exposure to moisture and heat, which affects garment fit.

learning_activity_name: Make informed decision on fabric type for different purposes basing on their properties
sla_name: Making informed decisions on fabric type based on properties
sla_assessment_criteria: Informed decision on fabric type for different purposes basing on their properties were well made.
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Selecting the right fabric for a specific purpose requires matching a fabric's tested properties to the practical demands of its intended use.
sla_notes_details: Making an informed decision on fabric type involves reviewing the results of fibre and fabric tests (fibre content, strength, colourfastness, shrinkage, absorbency) alongside practical requirements such as comfort, durability, care requirements, cost and appearance for the intended purpose (for example, school uniforms, sportswear, bedding or ceremonial garments). A fabric with high absorbency and softness suits everyday comfortable clothing, while a fabric with high tensile strength and low pilling suits workwear or uniforms subject to heavy use and frequent washing. Balancing these factors against budget and availability leads to a sound, informed fabric choice.
sla_notes_illustrations: When selecting fabric for school uniforms, a decision-maker would prioritise high tensile strength and good colourfastness (since uniforms are washed frequently and worn daily) over a fabric that is very soft but weak and prone to fading.
sla_notes_daily_life: Parents choosing durable, easy-to-wash fabric for children's school uniforms, and hospitals choosing colourfast, strong fabric for uniforms, make these same informed decisions based on fabric properties.
sla_exercise: Name two factors considered when making an informed decision on fabric type.::Durability (strength) and colourfastness (or comfort, cost, care requirements).||Why would a fabric with high tensile strength and low pilling be chosen for a school uniform?::Because uniforms are washed and worn frequently, so the fabric must resist tearing and keep a neat appearance over time.||What must be balanced against fabric performance when making a fabric choice?::Cost and availability of the fabric.

sla_name: Designing and making household articles using embroidery, applique and quilt techniques
sla_assessment_criteria: Household articles using embroidery, applique and quilts techniques were well designed and made.
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Household textile articles such as cushion covers, table cloths and quilts can be both functional and decorative when made using traditional needlework techniques.
sla_notes_details: Designing a household article begins with selecting the item (such as a cushion cover, table runner or quilt), planning a design suited to embroidery (stitched thread patterns), applique (attached fabric pieces forming a design) or quilting (stitched, padded layers forming a textured pattern), and choosing appropriate fabric, thread and, for quilting, wadding or batting. The article is then constructed by cutting the base fabric to size, transferring the design, executing the chosen decorative technique carefully and evenly, and finishing edges neatly (hemming or binding) so the article is both attractive and durable for household use.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student designing an embroidered cushion cover would sketch a simple floral motif onto the fabric, stitch it using satin and stem stitches in coloured thread, then sew the finished front panel to a plain back panel to complete a usable cushion cover.
sla_notes_daily_life: Hand-embroidered table cloths, appliqued cushion covers and patchwork quilts sold in local markets or made by families at home are everyday products of these same decorative textile techniques.
sla_exercise: Name three techniques used to design and make decorated household articles.::Embroidery, applique and quilting.||What material is typically added between fabric layers in a quilted article?::Wadding or batting, to create a padded, textured effect.||Why should the edges of a household textile article be neatly hemmed or bound?::To make the article durable and give it a neat, finished appearance for household use.

sla_name: Designing a potential Tanzanian national dress based on traditional designs
sla_assessment_criteria: A potential Tanzanian national dress basing on traditional designs were well designed.
sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: This competence challenges students to synthesise their knowledge of Tanzania's diverse traditional garments into an original design proposal for a unifying national dress.
sla_notes_details: Designing a potential Tanzanian national dress involves reviewing traditional features from multiple Tanzanian ethnic groups studied earlier (materials, colours, patterns, silhouette), identifying elements that could represent national identity broadly rather than one specific group, and combining these thoughtfully into an original design that respects cultural heritage while being practical for modern wear. The process includes sketching design illustrations, selecting suitable fabric and colours (which might draw on national symbols such as the Tanzanian flag colours), and presenting the design with an explanation of which traditional influences were used and why.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student might design a national dress combining a kitenge-style printed fabric in the green, black, blue and yellow of the Tanzanian flag with a draped silhouette inspired by coastal Swahili dress, presenting sketches that explain each cultural influence chosen.
sla_notes_daily_life: National dress design competitions and cultural events in Tanzania that showcase garments representing the nation's shared identity reflect exactly this same creative and cultural design process.
sla_exercise: What is the goal of designing a potential Tanzanian national dress?::To create an original garment design that represents national identity by combining features from multiple traditional Tanzanian designs.||Name one source of inspiration a student might use when designing a national dress.::Traditional ethnic garment features (or national symbols such as flag colours).||What should accompany the design illustrations when presenting a proposed national dress?::An explanation of which traditional influences were used and why.

sla_assessment_criteria: Garment parts using CAD/CAM software were well designed.

sla_references: TET(2023), TEXTILES AND GARMENT CONSTRUCTION SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Designing individual garment parts digitally allows precise drafting and easy adjustment before any fabric is cut, saving time and material.
sla_notes_details: Designing garment parts using CAD/CAM software involves selecting the garment component to design (such as a sleeve, collar, bodice or pocket), using the software's drafting tools to create the pattern piece to accurate measurements, adding necessary details such as seam allowances, darts, notches and grainlines, and adjusting the design digitally for fit or style changes without redrawing from scratch. Once finalised, the digital pattern can be printed onto paper or cardboard as a physical template for cutting fabric, or sent directly to a computer-controlled cutting machine for production.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student designing a sleeve using CAD software could quickly adjust the sleeve's width and length using digital measurement tools, then print the finalised pattern piece onto card to use as a cutting template, without having to hand-draft the pattern again for each size change.
sla_notes_daily_life: Modern garment factories and design studios in the textile industry use CAD/CAM software exactly this way to design and mass-produce accurate pattern pieces efficiently.
sla_exercise: Name one garment part that can be designed using CAD/CAM software.::A sleeve (or collar, bodice, pocket).||What details must be added to a digital garment pattern besides its basic shape?::Seam allowances, darts, notches and grainlines.||What is one advantage of designing garment parts digitally rather than by hand?::Design changes can be made quickly and precisely without redrawing the whole pattern from scratch.

sla_notes_intro: The Form VI portfolio brings together the full range of practical textile work completed across both years, including more advanced decorative and design techniques.
sla_notes_details: Preparing this portfolio involves collecting samples of embroidered, applique and quilted work, along with garment patterns developed using CAD/CAM software and any other prototypes created during the course, organising them to show a clear progression in skill from simpler to more advanced techniques, mounting and labelling each item clearly with the technique and purpose, and presenting the complete collection professionally, ready for final assessment. The portfolio should demonstrate mastery across both traditional hand techniques and modern digital design methods covered in the syllabus.
sla_notes_illustrations: A Form VI student's final portfolio might include an embroidered sample, a piece of quilted household fabric, a printed CAD-designed garment pattern, and a national dress design sketch, arranged to show the full range of skills developed from Form V through Form VI.
sla_notes_daily_life: Just as a tailor or textile designer maintains a portfolio of finished samples to show clients the breadth of their skill, this final school portfolio prepares students to present their own capabilities professionally.
